The mechanism is fully established from source; the few points that would need execution to confirm are flagged at the end.\n\n## Background: the intended lifecycle\n\n- **Normal write**: `SegmentImpl::Insert` (`src/db/index/segment/segment.cc:903-917`) calls `append_wal(doc)` first, which **lazily opens the member `wal_file_`** (`segment.cc:4324-4340` → `open_wal_file()`, `segment.cc:4303-4322`), then applies the doc in memory via `internal_insert` (`segment.cc:837-880`).\n- **Persistence**: `SegmentImpl::flush()` (`segment.cc:2217-2324`) is the *only* path that dumps the in-memory forward store, registers persisted blocks in the segment meta (`finish_memory_components`, `segment.cc:4342`), commits a new version (`update_version`, `segment.cc:4414`), and then **removes the WAL** (`segment.cc:2305-2315`).\n- **Crash recovery**: on open, `SegmentImpl::Open` calls `recover()` **only if the segment meta still carries a `writing_forward_block`** (`segment.cc:485-501`). `recover()` (`segment.cc:4193-4301`) replays the WAL into memory.\n\n## 1. State that differs between recovery and ordinary insertion\n\n`recover()` opens the WAL through a **separate local handle** `recover_wal_file` (`segment.cc:4206-4214`), replays each record through `internal_insert/internal_update/internal_upsert/internal_delete` (`segment.cc:4250-4272`), bumps `mem_block.max_doc_id_` (`segment.cc:4285-4288`), and closes the local handle via `AILEGO_DEFER` (`segment.cc:4216`). **It never assigns the member `wal_file_`**, and the only opener of `wal_file_` is `append_wal` (`segment.cc:4327-4330`), which runs only on a *new* write.\n\nSo after recovery the segment is in a state the ordinary path never produces:\n\n| | ordinary insert session | post-recovery, no new writes |\n|---|---|---|\n| in-memory data (memory_store_, indexers, `doc_ids_`, id_map) | dirty | dirty (replayed) |\n| member `wal_file_` | non-null, `has_record()` true (`local_wal_file.h:75-77`) | **`nullptr`** |\n| on-disk durability | WAL records | WAL records only |\n\nReads still work because they are served entirely from the replayed in-memory state: `doc_count()` is `doc_ids_.size()` minus deletes (`segment.cc:589-599`), `internal_insert` populated `memory_store_`, the in-memory indexers, and `id_map_->upsert` (`segment.cc:853-878`), and `Stats()`/`Fetch` go through `get_all_segments()` which includes the writing segment (`src/db/collection.cc:403-425`, `2076-2086`). The replay trigger for the *next* open — the `writing_forward_block` in the committed version — is also still intact at this point.\n\n## 2. Call sequence and exact condition of the loss\n\n1. `CollectionImpl::Optimize` (`collection.cc:779-915`) sees `writing_segment_->doc_count() != 0` and calls `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing()` (`collection.cc:794-800`; body at `1517-1553`).\n2. That calls `writing_segment_->dump()` (`collection.cc:1519`) → `SegmentImpl::dump()` (`segment.cc:2197-2216`) → `flush()` — which hits the early return:\n\n   ```cpp\n   if (wal_file_ == nullptr || !wal_file_->has_record()) {\n     return Status::OK();                       // segment.cc:2220-2222\n   }\n   ```\n\n   **Exact condition: `wal_file_ == nullptr` because no write op occurred since the reopen.** `flush()` uses \"this process never opened the WAL handle\" as a proxy for \"nothing to persist\". With N replayed docs pending, it returns OK having done *nothing*: no `memory_store_->flush()`, no `finish_memory_components()` (which would register the forward/vector blocks in the meta, `segment.cc:4342-4412`), no `update_version()`, and no WAL removal (`segment.cc:2305-2315`). `dump()` then seals successfully (`segment.cc:2205-2214`).\n3. `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing` proceeds: registers the old segment as persisted (`collection.cc:1522`), creates a fresh empty writing segment (`1527-1532`), then **`writing_segment_meta->remove_writing_forward_block()` (`collection.cc:1538`)**, adds the meta to the version (`1539`), and durably commits it (`version_manager_->apply` + `flush`, `collection.cc:1546-1548`; `version_manager.cc:260, 282`). This commit **destroys the only trigger that would ever replay the WAL again**, while step 2 never moved the data anywhere else.\n4. The compact phase succeeds trivially: for one small segment, `build_compact_task` emits a single `CreateVectorIndexTask` (`collection.cc:~990-1002`) → `create_all_vector_index` (`segment_helper.cc:1113-1125`, `segment.cc:1617-1640`). FLAT fields are already marked indexed at `Create` time so the task skips (`segment.cc:1685-1690`); for HNSW-style fields it merges the *persisted* indexers `vector_indexers_[column]` — empty, because `finish_memory_components` never moved the memory indexers — and `VectorColumnIndexer::Merge` **returns OK on empty input** (`vector_column_indexer.cc:111-113`), writing at most an empty index file that is registered with the in-memory doc count (`segment.cc:1711-1727`). `Optimize` returns OK.\n5. **Reopen**: `CollectionImpl::recovery` (`collection.cc:1836-1892`) opens the old segment from the committed version. `SegmentImpl::Open` finds no `writing_forward_block` and takes the else branch (`segment.cc:502-511`) — `recover()` is never called. The WAL file `<col>/<seg_id>/<block_id>.wal` (path per `file_helper.h:74-79`) still physically exists (its removal was inside the skipped `flush()` body), but it is permanently orphaned. `doc_ids_` is rebuilt solely from persisted SCALAR blocks (`load_persist_scalar_blocks`, `segment.cc:3913-3960`) — none contain the recovered docs — so `doc_count()==0` and pk fetches miss (the id_map was never re-flushed either; `segment.cc:2266-2269` skipped).\n\nThe control case never breaks because ordinary inserts keep `wal_file_` non-null with records, so `dump()→flush()` executes the full persistence path and removes the WAL *before* the version commit. Similarly, a single insert after recovery would re-arm `append_wal`/`open_wal_file` and mask the bug — matching the scenario's \"without inserting any additional documents.\"\n\n## 3. Why success and same-handle statistics prove nothing\n\n- The no-op is **reported as success**: the early return yields `Status::OK()` (`segment.cc:2221`), which `dump()`, `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing`, and `Optimize` all propagate. Even an explicit `CollectionImpl::Flush()` after pure recovery is the same silent no-op (`collection.cc:380-395` → `writing_segment_->flush()`).\n- Every same-handle observation reads **process-local memory**, not disk: `Stats()` sums `doc_count()` over live segment objects (`collection.cc:403-425`), `doc_count()` is `doc_ids_.size()` (`segment.cc:589-599`), and the sealed old segment stays registered in `segment_manager_` (`collection.cc:1522`) with `memory_store_`, indexers, and `doc_ids_` untouched (the code that would close/reset them, `finish_memory_components`, never ran). Durability in this design is established only by *persisted blocks + committed version + WAL retained under a writing block*; `optimize()` destroyed the third element without ever creating the first, and no in-process statistic observes any of the three.\n\n## 4. Smallest repair principle and regression test (described, not implemented)\n\n**Repair principle**: `flush()`'s \"clean\" predicate must reflect *actual unpersisted state*, not whether this process happens to hold an open WAL handle. The smallest change that restores the intended lifecycle: after WAL replay in `SegmentImpl::Open`/`recover()` (or whenever `Open` finds an existing WAL for the writing block), attach the member handle by calling `open_wal_file()` (it reopens with `create_new=false` and seeks to end, `local_wal_file.cc:92-106`), so `has_record()` is true. The existing `flush()` body then does everything correctly — persist blocks, commit version, remove WAL — and `dump()`/`close()`/`Optimize`/`Flush` all become sound with no other changes. An equivalent alternative is an explicit dirty flag set by `recover()` and cleared at the end of `flush()`, consulted at `segment.cc:2220`. The mechanism is fully established from source; the few points that would need execution to confirm are flagged at the end.\n\n## Background: the intended lifecycle\n\n- **Normal write**: `SegmentImpl::Insert` (`src/db/index/segment/segment.cc:903-917`) calls `append_wal(doc)` first, which **lazily opens the member `wal_file_`** (`segment.cc:4324-4340` → `open_wal_file()`, `segment.cc:4303-4322`), then applies the doc in memory via `internal_insert` (`segment.cc:837-880`).\n- **Persistence**: `SegmentImpl::flush()` (`segment.cc:2217-2324`) is the *only* path that dumps the in-memory forward store, registers persisted blocks in the segment meta (`finish_memory_components`, `segment.cc:4342`), commits a new version (`update_version`, `segment.cc:4414`), and then **removes the WAL** (`segment.cc:2305-2315`).\n- **Crash recovery**: on open, `SegmentImpl::Open` calls `recover()` **only if the segment meta still carries a `writing_forward_block`** (`segment.cc:485-501`). `recover()` (`segment.cc:4193-4301`) replays the WAL into memory.\n\n## 1. State that differs between recovery and ordinary insertion\n\n`recover()` opens the WAL through a **separate local handle** `recover_wal_file` (`segment.cc:4206-4214`), replays each record through `internal_insert/internal_update/internal_upsert/internal_delete` (`segment.cc:4250-4272`), bumps `mem_block.max_doc_id_` (`segment.cc:4285-4288`), and closes the local handle via `AILEGO_DEFER` (`segment.cc:4216`). **It never assigns the member `wal_file_`**, and the only opener of `wal_file_` is `append_wal` (`segment.cc:4327-4330`), which runs only on a *new* write.\n\nSo after recovery the segment is in a state the ordinary path never produces:\n\n| | ordinary insert session | post-recovery, no new writes |\n|---|---|---|\n| in-memory data (memory_store_, indexers, `doc_ids_`, id_map) | dirty | dirty (replayed) |\n| member `wal_file_` | non-null, `has_record()` true (`local_wal_file.h:75-77`) | **`nullptr`** |\n| on-disk durability | WAL records | WAL records only |\n\nReads still work because they are served entirely from the replayed in-memory state: `doc_count()` is `doc_ids_.size()` minus deletes (`segment.cc:589-599`), `internal_insert` populated `memory_store_`, the in-memory indexers, and `id_map_->upsert` (`segment.cc:853-878`), and `Stats()`/`Fetch` go through `get_all_segments()` which includes the writing segment (`src/db/collection.cc:403-425`, `2076-2086`). Call sequence and exact condition of the loss\n\n1. `CollectionImpl::Optimize` (`collection.cc:779-915`) sees `writing_segment_->doc_count() != 0` and calls `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing()` (`collection.cc:794-800`; body at `1517-1553`).\n2. With N replayed docs pending, it returns OK having done *nothing*: no `memory_store_->flush()`, no `finish_memory_components()` (which would register the forward/vector blocks in the meta, `segment.cc:4342-4412`), no `update_version()`, and no WAL removal (`segment.cc:2305-2315`). `dump()` then seals successfully (`segment.cc:2205-2214`).\n3. `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing` proceeds: registers the old segment as persisted (`collection.cc:1522`), creates a fresh empty writing segment (`1527-1532`), then **`writing_segment_meta->remove_writing_forward_block()` (`collection.cc:1538`)**, adds the meta to the version (`1539`), and durably commits it (`version_manager_->apply` + `flush`, `collection.cc:1546-1548`; `version_manager.cc:260, 282`). This commit **destroys the only trigger that would ever replay the WAL again**, while step 2 never moved the data anywhere else.\n4. The compact phase succeeds trivially: for one small segment, `build_compact_task` emits a single `CreateVectorIndexTask` (`collection.cc:~990-1002`) → `create_all_vector_index` (`segment_helper.cc:1113-1125`, `segment.cc:1617-1640`). FLAT fields are already marked indexed at `Create` time so the task skips (`segment.cc:1685-1690`); for HNSW-style fields it merges the *persisted* indexers `vector_indexers_[column]` — empty, because `finish_memory_components` never moved the memory indexers — and `VectorColumnIndexer::Merge` **returns OK on empty input** (`vector_column_indexer.cc:111-113`), writing at most an empty index file that is registered with the in-memory doc count (`segment.cc:1711-1727`). `Optimize` returns OK.\n5. **Reopen**: `CollectionImpl::recovery` (`collection.cc:1836-1892`) opens the old segment from the committed version. `SegmentImpl::Open` finds no `writing_forward_block` and takes the else branch (`segment.cc:502-511`) — `recover()` is never called. The WAL file `<col>/<seg_id>/<block_id>.wal` (path per `file_helper.h:74-79`) still physically exists (its removal was inside the skipped `flush()` body), but it is permanently orphaned. `doc_ids_` is rebuilt solely from persisted SCALAR blocks (`load_persist_scalar_blocks`, `segment.cc:3913-3960`) — none contain the recovered docs — so `doc_count()==0` and pk fetches miss (the id_map was never re-flushed either; `segment.cc:2266-2269` skipped).\n\nThe control case never breaks because ordinary inserts keep `wal_file_` non-null with records, so `dump()→flush()` executes the full persistence path and removes the WAL *before* the version commit. Similarly, a single insert after recovery would re-arm `append_wal`/`open_wal_file` and mask the bug — matching the scenario's \"without inserting any additional documents.\"\n\n## 3. Why success and same-handle statistics prove nothing\n\n- The no-op is **reported as success**: the early return yields `Status::OK()` (`segment.cc:2221`), which `dump()`, `switch_to_new_segment_for_writing`, and `Optimize` all propagate. Even an explicit `CollectionImpl::Flush()` after pure recovery is the same silent no-op (`collection.cc:380-395` → `writing_segment_->flush()`).\n- Every same-handle observation reads **process-local memory**, not disk: `Stats()` sums `doc_count()` over live segment objects (`collection.cc:403-425`), `doc_count()` is `doc_ids_.size()` (`segment.cc:589-599`), and the sealed old segment stays registered in `segment_manager_` (`collection.cc:1522`) with `memory_store_`, indexers, and `doc_ids_` untouched (the code that would close/reset them, `finish_memory_components`, never ran). Durability in this design is established only by *persisted blocks + committed version + WAL retained under a writing block*; `optimize()` destroyed the third element without ever creating the first, and no in-process statistic observes any of the three.\n\n## 4. The existing `flush()` body then does everything correctly — persist blocks, commit version, remove WAL — and `dump()`/`close()`/`Optimize`/`Flush` all become sound with no other changes.
